excerpt: Olostep is a web data API for AI agents: search, scrape, crawl, answer and monitor the web through one API. Free trial, plans from $9/month, and how it compares with Firecrawl.
content:
Olostep sells web access for AI agents as an API. Its endpoints cover scraping a page into clean Markdown, HTML, JSON or a screenshot; crawling every page of a site; mapping a site's URLs; searching the web in natural language and getting ranked links; getting an AI-written answer from web sources; batch jobs, which the company says process up to 100,000 URLs in 5–7 minutes; and monitors that watch for changes such as a new blog post or a price change. Every request is rendered with JavaScript and uses residential IP addresses, according to its pricing page. There is also an MCP server and CLI for coding agents, and an agent that runs web research from a prompt.

Asked on Product Hunt how it differs from other scraping tools, co-founder Hamza Ali said Olostep works with most other providers rather than competing with them, acting as a layer on top in the way Cursor sits on top of models. The company behind it is Olostep Technologies Inc.

Olostep launched on Product Hunt on 30 August 2026 and finished #3 for the day, with 222 upvotes and 19 comments (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Olostep ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing and About pages and its Product Hunt page, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Web search, scraping, crawling and monitoring API built for AI agents

gallery.alt: Olostep 'Infrastructure for the Web's second user' with a URL box and scrape, crawl, map, search and answer options
Olostep 'Let your agents search, answer and explore': a query answered from several news sources
Olostep 'Works with all the tools you already use' showing coding agents and frameworks such as Cursor, Claude and LangChain

use_cases: Turning web pages into clean Markdown or JSON for an AI app
Crawling a documentation site to feed a knowledge base
Letting a coding agent search and read the web through MCP
Watching competitor pages for price or content changes
Processing large batches of URLs for data pipelines

paragraphs: Hunter Rohan Chaubey introduced Olostep with the idea that AI agents are becoming the web's second user, yet still reach it like humans do: opening tabs, fighting JavaScript, parsing messy HTML and maintaining brittle scrapers.
Co-founder Arslan Ali added that the team is building web data infrastructure for AI, on the belief that the web is where businesses run and knowledge lives, and agents are its new consumers.
launch_story.attribution: Rohan Chaubey (hunter) and Arslan Ali, co-founder, on Product Hunt

fit: build AI agents or apps that need fresh web data
process large numbers of URLs and care about cost per request
want search, scraping and change monitoring in one API
not_fit: need data from one site with an official API: use that API
want a no-code tool: Olostep is aimed at developers
want volume tiers on the Product Hunt page: a reviewer noted you have to click through to the site

pricing.intro: Olostep has a free trial, monthly plans by request volume and prepaid credit packs. Prices are Olostep's, in US dollars.

plans.name: Trial
plans.detail: 500 successful requests, low rate limits, no credit card

plans.name: Scale
plans.detail: 1 million successful requests, AI-powered browser automations

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Custom discounts at very high volume

notes: Credit packs for spiky usage: 10,000 credits for $20, 250,000 for $200, 2 million for $1,000, valid for six months.
Plans are pro-rated if you switch.

pros: Free trial without a card and a low $9 entry plan
Search, scrape, crawl, answer and monitor in one API
JavaScript rendering and residential IPs on every request
MCP server and CLI for coding agents
cons: Developer-focused; no no-code interface for most features
Low rate limits on the free trial
Credit packs expire after six months

liked: Natural-language search on top of scrape and crawl
Built-in monitoring instead of a scraper plus a cron job
asked: How it differs from other scraping tools (it works with other providers as a layer on top)
How the Monitor API decides what counts as a real change
criticised: Pricing tiers are not shown on the Product Hunt page

quotes.text: The natural language query angle on Olostep felt like a genuine different approach rather than just another scrape endpoint.
quotes.author: Gal Dayan (4/5 review)

quotes.text: Diffing a page is easy, deciding what counts as a change is the actual problem.
quotes.author: Rabnoor Singh

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as Olostep alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.what: Web data API for AI agents and developers
items.difference: The better-known name in the same category; a reviewer chose Olostep for its natural-language search.

items.name: Browserbase
items.difference: Gives agents full browsers to drive; Olostep returns ready-made data through API endpoints.

items.name: Browser Use
items.what: Makes websites usable by AI agents
items.difference: Focused on agents operating websites step by step rather than bulk data extraction.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Tabstack by Mozilla and Reworkd.

x.none: We have not linked posts about Olostep on X yet.

faq.a: A web data API for AI agents with endpoints to scrape, crawl, map, search, answer and monitor the web, plus an MCP server and CLI.
A free trial includes 500 requests. Starter is $9 a month for 5,000 requests, Standard $99 for 200,000 and Scale $399 for 1 million. Credit packs start at $20 for 10,000 credits.

faq.q: How is Olostep different from Firecrawl?
faq.a: Both turn web pages into data for AI. Olostep's co-founder said it works on top of other providers rather than competing with them, and a reviewer singled out its natural-language search.

faq.q: Can Olostep monitor web pages for changes?
faq.a: Yes. Its Monitor API watches for events such as a new blog post or a page change.
